answer: Trust scores decay exponentially with a fixed half-life, so an identity must provide sustained, reciprocated honest service to retain influence. EigenTrust-style centrality propagates trust through weighted paths, while reciprocity-weighted transitivity limits gains from collusive links. A freshly spawned sybil has almost no trusted incoming support: its centrality is near zero, leaving a hollow network claim that cannot meet consensus thresholds. A harbor of established peers cannot instantly transfer trust across that delta.
